note: GLOBALCIT's Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (EUI, 2025), coding the law in force on 1 January 2024 (A06a Const 123(1), 126, Sections 16-17, Third Schedule; A06b Const 123(1), 126, Sections 16-17, Third Schedule; L05 Const 134(1)(a)): ordinary naturalisation after 10 years' residence; the applicant must give up other citizenships; a citizen loses the citizenship on voluntarily taking another. Reforms after that date are checked in the file's later sources, where a later source is given. Citizenship at birth is read from the same dataset's 2024 coding of modes A01a (descent, born in country: Generally applicable provision), A01b (descent, born abroad: Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship), A02a (birth in country: No provision) and A02b (birth in country to a parent born there: No provision), as its codebook (RSC/GLOBALCIT 2025/01, sections 3.2.1a to 3.2.2b) defines them: not by birth in the territory alone (provisions for foundlings and children otherwise stateless, modes A03a and A03b, aren't held by the form); by descent from either parent, a child born abroad on the limit the dataset states. Changes to the law at birth after 1 January 2024 weren't checked for this file.

sources.title: GLOBALCIT Citizenship Law Dataset v3.0 (Vink, van der Baaren, Bauböck, Dzankic, Honohan, Manby; EUI Research Data, 2025), country-year-mode files, Singapore, 2024
sources.said: Person has been resident in Singapore for 12 months immediately prior to the application, and was resident in the country for 10 out of 12 years prior to the application. ... Renunciation of citizenship of another country required. ... Person acquired citizenship of another country by a voluntary and formal act other than by marriage. ... Generally applicable provision ... Person is born in Singapore to a citizen. Unless born to a father who is a foreign diplomat, or to a father who is an enemy alien and the child was born in a place then under occupation by the enemy. ... Generational transmission restriction: conditional on birthplace/place of residence /mode under which parent acquired citizenship ... Person is born to a citizen by birth, registration or descent. Citizenship is not acquired if the child is not registered within 1 year after birth, or if the child acquired the citizenship of the country of birth and the parent is a citizen by registration. In case the parent is a citizen by descent, the parent needs to have resided in Singapore prior to the person's birth for a total of 5 years or for 2 out of the 5 years immediately preceding the person's birth. ... No provision ... No provision

atBirth.descentAbroad: Person is born to a citizen by birth, registration or descent. Citizenship is not acquired if the child is not registered within 1 year after birth, or if the child acquired the citizenship of the country of birth and the parent is a citizen by registration. In case the parent is a citizen by descent, the parent needs to have resided in Singapore prior to the person's birth for a total of 5 years or for 2 out of the 5 years immediately preceding the person's birth.
